# 太子慕魄經

**ID:** T0167
**Volume:** T03
**Category:** 本緣部類
**Original Category:** 本緣部
**Byline:** 後漢 安世高譯
**Dynasty:** 東漢
**Date:** 148–170
**Juans:** 1
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T0167

## Contributors
- 安清 (A000366)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A short single-fascicle Eastern-Hàn *jātaka* recounting the past life of the Buddha as Prince Mùpò 慕魄 (the name's Indic source debated; conventionally read as a transliteration of \*Mūka, "the Mute"), a king's son who feigned muteness and immobility for thirteen years to avoid worldly rule, until his father, despairing of his apparent disability, ordered him buried. The *jātaka* is one of the canonical Buddhist *bodhisattva*-renunciation narratives and is paralleled in the *Mūgapakkhajātaka* (Pāli *Jātaka* no. 538). Signature: 「後漢安息三藏安世高譯」.

The Taishō header cross-references [T152(38)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0001) ([康僧會](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BA%B7%E5%83%A7%E6%9C%83) Kāng Sēnghuì's parallel) and [T168](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0020) ([竺法護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E6%B3%95%E8%AD%B7) Dharmarakṣa's parallel translation).

**Abstract**

T167 is a securely-attributed [安世高](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E4%B8%96%E9%AB%98) Ān Shìgāo translation, dated to his Luòyáng period 148–170 CE. The text is paralleled by [竺法護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E6%B3%95%E8%AD%B7) Dharmarakṣa's later *[Tàizǐ Mùpò jīng (T168)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0020)* and by [康僧會](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BA%B7%E5%83%A7%E6%9C%83) Kāng Sēnghuì's narrative version in [T152](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0001); the three Chinese versions of the same Indic *jātaka* have been a key test-case for the development of Chinese Buddhist *jātaka*-translation idiom across the Hàn / Western-Jìn / Wú periods. The Pāli parallel (*Mūgapakkha* / *Temiya-jātaka*) is the source-narrative for the Thai *Mahānipāta* dance-drama tradition; the Chinese versions thus preserve an early form of one of the most widely diffused Buddhist *jātaka*s.
